_about: The Martin Marprelate tracts (1588-1589), anonymous Puritan satires against the bishops, in John Petheram's 'Puritan Discipline Tracts' reprints from the black-letter originals, with introductions and notes (London: Petheram, 1842-1845): the Epistle, the Epitome and Hay any Worke for Cooper. Also two histories of the controversy: William Maskell's (London: Pickering, 1845, hostile to Martin) and William Pierce's Historical Introduction to the Marprelate Tracts (London: Constable, 1908). The name check is on 'Marprelate', the tracts' own pseudonym. Internet Archive OCR, raw and unconverted; each title page read before listing.

marprelate-epistle-1842: An Epistle to the Terrible Priests of the Convocation House (London: Petheram, 1842)
marprelate-epitome-1843: An Epitome of the First Book of Dr. John Bridges' Defence (London: Petheram, 1843; Google scan)
marprelate-hay-any-worke-1845: Hay any Worke for Cooper (London: Petheram, 1845)
maskell-marprelate-history-1845: William Maskell, A History of the Martin Marprelate Controversy in the Reign of Queen Elizabeth (London: Pickering, 1845)
pierce-marprelate-introduction-1908: William Pierce, An Historical Introduction to the Marprelate Tracts (London: Constable, 1908)
